headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: ctx observes Claude Code events while ChatGPT Desktop ingests files/screenshots, creating a default trust-bridge with limited provenance controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps, while ctx observes Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and handles MCP-related entities. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled output from one side can be reinterpreted by the other, though the exact default path is not fully documented.
conditions: IF ctx forwards Claude Code event content into prompts or files that ChatGPT Desktop reads
IF ChatGPT Desktop treats file or app content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of ctx-observed event payloads into ChatGPT prompts
Require explicit human review before copying any agent output between tools
Tag all bridged content with source provenance in filenames or headers
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance filtering between Claude Code events and downstream prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch filesystem-backed content: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files and supported macOS app files, while ctx uses filesystem and logs/harness records. If they share a workspace, sensitive material can flow from A into B outputs or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared directory by default, so this is medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or project directory
IF uploaded files or logs contain sensitive data classes
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory
Restrict ctx logs from storing file contents
Avoid uploading secrets or regulated data to shared workspaces
Rotate or redact logs after each run
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read-only filesystem access and vendor-only network egress, while ctx can install packages, run browsers, and write to filesystem. Their capabilities overlap on filesystem access and external APIs, so concurrent use can conflict on shared mutable resources even though ChatGPT itself cannot write files.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem tree
IF ctx modifies files that ChatGPT Desktop is simultaneously reading
mitigations: Serialize edits to shared files
Use file locks or a single-writer convention
Keep ChatGPT Desktop in read-only review mode
Run ctx in a separate clone of the repository
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx observes Claude Code events and can act on agent entities, while ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files and app context. If ctx treats ChatGPT-generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream automation or logs. The profiles show a plausible chain but not a fully documented default action path, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF ctx uses ChatGPT output as a source of truth without verification
IF downstream automation consumes ctx-updated records or logs
mitigations: Require a verification step before ctx records ChatGPT output
Mark ChatGPT-derived content as untrusted until checked
Limit downstream actions to read-only reporting
Review any generated actions before execution
requires-engineering: add confidence gates to ctx pipelines

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile. The main compliance concern is that ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and app content, while ctx stores audit/runtime logs and graph data; if regulated data is placed into both, policy alignment must be checked. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise data flow, not a single-agent violation.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into ChatGPT Desktop and also persisted in ctx logs or graph data
IF organizational policy requires retention or residency controls not stated in either profile
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Review retention settings for both tools
Redact logs before storage
Separate compliance-sensitive projects from general automation
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
